solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extremely anxious before son gets first aid

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of anxious
S is the standard abbreviation for son
first is written 1st, with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A nervous person makes sure their son is the first one to receive medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' reads as one phrase, but 'first' belongs to the wordplay and 'aid' stands alone as the definition. 1ST becomes IST because the digit 1 looks like an I.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, so the verb is a straightforward synonym of aid.

clue.text: Refuse to vote for a ban -it's wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician declines to back a proposed ban because they think it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to choose not to cast a vote either way, which is declining to vote.

clue.text: Only receiving Italian broadcast of game

indicators.note: something receiving goods takes them inside it, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Only an Italian channel is showing this particular game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiving' makes the only word hold the other two, splitting it before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a card or peg game played by one person alone.

clue.text: Inflexible Republican leaves with an award leaving a stink

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: stern means strict and unbending
R is the abbreviation for Republican, removed here
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A hardline Republican quits, collects an honour, and departs amid a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour (CH) is a British order awarded for achievement in the arts, science or public life.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul smell, so it is a synonym of a stink.

clue.text: Remains occupied by Central America after Foreign Office prediction

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
the rest is what remains
CA is the abbreviation for Central America

explanation.surface: Diplomats forecast that leftover forces will be stationed in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a noun for leftovers or a corpse but is used here for what is left over, the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what will happen, which is a prediction.

clue.text: About to get caught out of position on the field

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
cover is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught out and the fielder was standing out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side; take away the C for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean about or concerning, as in arguing over money.

clue.text: Unconventional priest about to withdraw self-indulgent activities

indicators.note: an unconventional arrangement is out of the normal order, so the letters are reshuffled
about means around, so the shuffled letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
to go is to leave or withdraw

explanation.surface: An unorthodox priest is about to retreat from his parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego trips are actions done chiefly to boost one's own self-importance, hence self-indulgent.

clue.text: Animated by a return of wickedness

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: A character is brought to life by a resurgence of villainy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'a return' does double duty in the surface but supplies the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive means lively and full of energy, which is what animated describes.

clue.text: Trial involving politician ending in case of a violent disturbance

indicators.note: a thing involving others includes them within itself
the ending of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a test is a trial
MP is a Member of Parliament
the final letter of case

explanation.surface: A court trial of a politician ends in a case of public violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in case' could read as a verdict; it just picks the last letter of case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and figuratively any violent disturbance or upheaval.

clue.text: Crack on edge of record made by you

indicators.note: the edge of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: to crack a code is to solve it
the first letter of record

explanation.surface: A crack on the rim of a vinyl record, caused by you.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the solver is 'you', the person tackling the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The reader of the clue is the person doing the puzzle, so 'you' refers to the solver.

clue.text: A university teacher is introduced to cannabis largely as pleasure-seeking

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the last letter is cut
something introduced to another is put inside it

blocks.note: hemp is the cannabis plant
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic gets into marijuana purely for the pleasure of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university lecturer, chiefly at Oxford or Cambridge; 'largely' trims the drug's other name before the rest goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure as the main aim of life.

clue.text: Scholarly study about real changes at the top

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
letters that change take a different order
in a down clue the top is the start, so this piece is placed first

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: An academic study about real changes taking place at the top of an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'at the top' means placed first, so the rearranged REAL comes before the reversed study.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) describes someone with deep academic knowledge, a synonym of scholarly.

clue.text: Stuck in a relationship

blocks.note: first meaning: fixed or fastened on
second meaning: romantically committed to someone

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue sounds like a complaint about a trapped partner; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both something physically fastened and a person who already has a partner.

clue.text: A novelist inexperienced on the radio

indicators.note: anything heard on the radio is only spoken, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: green means new and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A first-time author nervously appears on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was the English novelist of Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene is an example of a novelist, so the general term covers him.

clue.text: Popular Communist leader supporting a protest on the outskirts of Tbilisi

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is taken
outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the first and last letters are kept
in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the rest

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
the first and last letters of Tbilisi
the first letter of Communist

explanation.surface: A well-liked party chief backs a demonstration on the edge of the Georgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means placed underneath, so the C comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for ordinary people, as in demotic speech, so it is close to popular.

clue.text: New Leicestershire opener holding excellent catch

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so just the initial letter is taken
to hold something is to have it within your grasp

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the first letter of Leicestershire
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A Leicestershire opening batsman, new to the side, holds on to a superb catch.
explanation.walkthrough: AI goes between N and L. Leicestershire is an English county with a first-class cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informally to catch or capture them.

clue.text: What Prospero promises to do when unimpeded by gin

definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as 'free (the) spirit'
an adjective phrase, read as 'free (of) spirit'

blocks.note: first reading: in The Tempest Prospero promises to release the airy spirit Ariel
second reading: gin is a spirit, and being without it is being free of spirit

explanation.walkthrough: Neither reading defines the everyday phrase for an independent person; both split the phrase into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero vows to liberate Ariel, a sprite, and gin is a distilled drink, so each reading puns on the phrase.

clue.text: Concerning an enquiry over soldiers sent north from base

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
one thing over another covers it, so it sits around the other piece

blocks.note: re means concerning
a probe is an investigation
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: An inquiry into soldiers being dispatched northwards from their camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like the military camp of the surface, but it is the definition, meaning morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, and base describes someone immoral and contemptible.

clue.text: Hurry to get money back after second favourite is withdrawn before Kelso's last

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word runs backwards
something withdrawn is pulled back, so it is read in reverse
the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
the final letter of Kelso
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A punter rushes to recover their stake when the second favourite is scratched before a race at Kelso.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelso is a racecourse in the Scottish Borders. The reversed money comes after the rest, which is why 'after' and 'before' frame the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom telling someone to hurry, from pressing hard on the accelerator.

clue.text: Plainly apparent without an article on work lacking restraint

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: overt means open and plainly visible
the is the definite article
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: It is obvious that a piece of writing is missing from a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, wrapping the first piece round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the top is an idiom for excessive or exaggerated behaviour, done without restraint.

clue.text: Revealed after all others survive

blocks.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
the last comes after all the others

explanation.surface: A secret revealed only once everyone else has had their say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all others' looks like a placing instruction but is a piece of wordplay itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to live or continue longer than them, which is surviving them.

clue.text: Begin with Frank

blocks.note: first meaning: to start something off
second meaning: candid and honest

explanation.surface: Instructions to start the proceedings with someone called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes Frank look like a man's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Open is a verb for starting something and an adjective for someone candid and straightforward.

clue.text: Some Huguenot Hal favoured very much

indicators.note: some of the words means just a part of them, so the letters lie within the run of text

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A French Protestant favoured Prince Hal a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Huguenots were French Protestants; Hal is Shakespeare's young Prince Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Not half is British slang meaning very much or extremely, as in 'Did you enjoy it? Not half!'

clue.text: Counsel for Dicky Davies

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer acting for someone called Dicky Davies.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky Davies was a British TV sports presenter, so 'Dicky' reads as a first name; it is British slang for shaky or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to give them guidance, which is to advise them.

clue.text: A short time before Penny is found in a debauched fellow's company

indicators.note: a thing found in another is located inside it

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time
a roué is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Shortly before, a woman called Penny is spotted in the company of a rake.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Penny look like a woman's name; it is the coin abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors or performers touring together.

clue.text: Blighter runs off with a furry animal

indicators.note: something that runs off goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: blighter and rotter are both old British words for a nasty person
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A scoundrel makes off with a fur-covered creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs off' looks like an escape; it tells you to remove the R for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is an aquatic mammal with thick, dense fur, an example of a furry animal.

clue.text: Man almost trapped in a mine somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
something trapped in a place is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine
Edmond is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man nearly stuck down a mine somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmond loses its last letter and sits inside PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Piedmont is a region of north-west Italy around Turin, so it is somewhere in the country.

clue.text: Fairy queen hiding in the middle of Epping

indicators.note: a thing hiding in another is concealed inside it
the middle of a word is its central letters only

blocks.note: the two central letters of Epping
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The fairy queen is hiding deep in Epping Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the north-east edge of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology, a word found mostly in crosswords.

clue.text: One present of a shirt overwhelms nurse

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone at an event whose shirt is too much for a nurse to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One present' sounds like a gift, but it means a person who is present.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone who attends, a person present at an event.

clue.text: Capital of Brown to include Irish amateur

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it within

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
a is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's capital, with money including an Irish amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Brown look like the former British prime minister; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Story heard after convert's escape

indicators.note: what is heard is only spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: to convert something is to turn it into something else
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale told of a religious convert's escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert's' reads as possessive, but the 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom meaning to turn round and run away, which is to escape.

clue.text: Concerning this brave man falling short against an enemy from the east

indicators.note: falling short means not reaching the end, so the last letter is dropped
in an across clue coming from the east means running right to left

blocks.note: a hero is a brave man
a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: On the subject of a courageous man who failed to hold off an enemy from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereof is a formal, legal word meaning of or about this document or matter.
